newsitem.title: USA: Top Dole strategist quits in campaign shakeup.
newsitem.headline: Top Dole strategist quits in campaign shakeup.

text.p: Don Sipple, a top strategist for Republican presidential nominee Bob Dole, has quit in a reorganization of Dole's campaign for the November election, Dole spokeswoman Christina Martin said on Wednesday.

Martin said another top Dole strategist, Mike Murphy, was expected to follow Sipple in leaving the campaign. Dole is 15 to 20 percentage points behind President Bill Clinton, the Democratic nominee, in polls.
Martin said the Dole campaign was adding three new outside strategists to beef up its television and advertising operations which have been handled by Sipple and Murphy.

She said it was a "friendly parting of the ways" by Sipple and the expected departure of Murphy. Both had been operating a company called New Century Media, which Martin said had been a free-standing operation but was now being integrated into the campaign.
Both Sipple and Murphy had an opportunity to stay with the campaign if they wanted to, she said.

In Dayton, Ohio, where Dole is campaigning, Dole press secretary Nelson Warfield said: "In order to enhance the coordination of the campaign as we move into the general election, a strategic decision was made to bring the ad group...more directly into the overall campaign structure under Scott Reed (the campaign manager)." He added: "Don and Mike (Sipple and Murphy) chose to go their own way and we part as friends."
